$meta.generatedFor: Jetpack Compose theme generation — values are literal, no aliases requiring resolution
$meta.note: Product name appears in tokens nowhere. A rename requires no token changes.
$meta.contrastPolicy: All text/background pairs listed meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 for >=24px). Ratios given against the surface each token is used on.
colorPolicy: The child's photo must be the most saturated element on any screen it appears on.
Pure red (status.destructive) appears in exactly one place: the delete-everything action. Nowhere else.
Degraded states use status.warning (burnt amber), never red, and always pair colour with an icon and a word.
State is never conveyed by colour alone.

surfaceMuted.comment: Non-target person rows, neutral info panels.

disabledInk.comment: Disabled label only. Never carries meaning alone.

accent.comment: Clay. Primary fill. 5.6:1 with white text.

scrim.comment: Soften overlay. Warm, never neutral grey.

scrimSheet.comment: Behind bottom sheets and system-dialog moments.

onAccent.comment: Dark ink on the light accent fill.

listening.comment: Sage. Calm, not 'success'. Always with a filled dot and the word.

paused.comment: Hollow dot. A parent's choice, so styled neutrally — never as a problem.

warning.comment: Burnt amber. Permission revoked, service killed, model failed, clip rejected. Serious, never shouty. Always carries an icon.

destructive.comment: The only red in the product. Delete-everything only.

locked.comment: Openable lock: lock_open_right glyph + an action.

unavailable.comment: Platform impossibility: block glyph, sunken row, NO control.

micDotAndroid.comment: Illustrative only — the real dot is drawn by the OS and cannot be styled or hidden.

serif.role: The voice. Only where a person is spoken to or about: the child's name, welcome headlines, the enrollment payoff, screen titles in emotional flows.

sans.role: The mechanics. Everything the app says about itself: settings, permissions, status, lists, all button labels.

families.rationale: IBM Plex Sans was chosen over Inter/Roboto because its official Hebrew sibling is drawn to the same skeleton — one type scale works in both scripts with no per-language tuning. Frank Ruhl Libre sits within ~2% of Source Serif's vertical metrics at the same optical size.

overlayName.comment: The largest type in the product. Block variant: 48/53.

titleSmall.comment: App bar title, person name in a card.

bodyLarge.comment: DEFAULT body size. The reader is distracted and one-handed.

hebrewAdjustments.comment: The ONLY per-script metric change: body line-height 1.55 -> 1.70. Sizes are identical across scripts. Hebrew is never bumped up to compensate for having no capitals.

rules: No fixed-height text containers. All cards and rows size to content.
Buttons grow vertically rather than truncating; label never ellipsises.
Icon+label rows wrap to a column above 1.6x.
The intervention overlay's photo shrinks (216 -> 160dp) before any text scales down; text never scales down.

xxl.use: around the one thing that matters on a screen

sheet.use: bottom sheets, the intervention photo card

radius.policy: Every button is a pill. It is the single cheapest decision separating this from a Material productivity app. Photos are circles everywhere except the intervention overlay, where the photo is a 24-radius rectangle — bigger, more present, more like a picture on a shelf.

e0.use: the page. Home sits here, mostly empty.

e2.comment: Dark elevation is carried by surface lightness, not shadow.

elevation.policy: Shadows are warm-tinted (brown), never neutral grey. Four levels and no more.

motion.policy: It breathes in. Nothing in this app snaps. The intervention arrives late by design, so its entrance must read as something arriving gently, never as an alarm catching up.

arrive.use: photo card entrance. No overshoot — overshoot reads as excitement.

overlayCardIn.comment: Starts after the scrim has begun, so the room dims first and the face arrives into it.

overlayEntranceTotal.comment: Deliberately at the slow end of comfortable.

overlayOut.comment: Leaving is brisk — the parent has already turned to their child.

audioDuckOut.comment: Ramped, never cut. A hard mute is startling.

secondChildFoldIn.properties: card grows; second avatar fades + slides 16dp inward
secondChildFoldIn.comment: Never a new layer stacked on top.

reducedMotion.properties: cross-fade only — no scale or translate anywhere
reducedMotion.comment: The overlay still FADES rather than cutting in. An instant cut is the one thing that would feel like an alarm.

afterFire.comment: One episode is one overlay, not a stutter. Does not re-trigger while the child keeps talking, and does not reappear immediately after a dismissal.

iconography.rationale: Rounded because the geometry is friendlier and matches the pill buttons. Weight 300 because the default 400 is too assertive next to this type.
iconography.filledUsage: Filled variants are used for exactly one thing: the active listening indicator.
iconography.policy: No icon ever carries meaning on its own — every one has a visible label beside it or an accessible name.

accessibility.redundantStateSignals: Listening status is carried by three signals at once: dot fill (solid vs hollow), colour, and words.
